_note: City facts for the planner and for grounding the AI guide. Travel times are approximate fastest typical journeys from Tokyo Station and must be checked against current timetables. Veg notes are general guidance, not claims about specific restaurants.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.season: Cherry blossom late March to early April; autumn colour in late November.
cities.culture: Shrines tucked between skyscrapers, Asakusa's old streets and Akihabara's pop culture in one city.
cities.veg: The widest choice in Japan: vegan ramen, Indian restaurants and plant-based cafés. Still ask about dashi in Japanese dishes.

cities.name: Kamakura
cities.season: Hydrangeas in June; easy day trip all year.
cities.culture: The Great Buddha, Zen temples and the sea, an hour from Tokyo. Enoshima's Benzaiten shrine is nearby.
cities.veg: Temple-style vegetarian cafés exist around the Zen temples; street snacks are often fish-based.

cities.name: Hakone
cities.season: Clear Fuji views most often in winter mornings.
cities.culture: Hot-spring inns, volcanic valleys and lake views of Mount Fuji.
cities.veg: Ryokan dinners are fish-heavy by default; most can prepare a vegetarian kaiseki if asked several days ahead.

cities.name: Nikko
cities.fromTokyo: About 2 h by Tobu limited express
cities.season: Autumn leaves in October are spectacular.
cities.culture: Ornate shrines in a cedar forest, waterfalls and mountain lakes.
cities.veg: Yuba (tofu skin) is the local speciality and is often vegetarian; ask whether the broth uses dashi.

cities.name: Kanazawa
cities.season: Snow-covered Kenroku-en garden in winter; lovely all year.
cities.culture: One of Japan's great gardens, samurai and geisha districts and gold-leaf craft.
cities.veg: Seafood dominates; look for fu (wheat gluten) dishes and Indian or vegan cafés near the station.

cities.name: Takayama
cities.season: Spring and autumn festivals; snowy villages nearby in winter.
cities.culture: An Edo-era old town in the Japanese Alps, close to Shirakawa-go and Hida-Furukawa.
cities.veg: Hida beef is everywhere, but hoba miso (miso grilled on a leaf) and mitarashi dango are good veg options; check for dashi.

cities.name: Kyoto
cities.season: Busiest during cherry blossom and autumn leaves; go early in the morning.
cities.culture: Over a thousand temples, Fushimi Inari's torii and three of the Indian-roots temples nearby.
cities.veg: Home of shojin ryori (Buddhist temple cuisine), which is traditionally plant-based, and of tofu restaurants near temples.

cities.name: Nara
cities.season: Easy day trip from Kyoto or Osaka all year.
cities.culture: Japan's first capital: the giant Buddha of Todai-ji and friendly bowing deer.
cities.veg: Temple towns offer shojin-style meals; kakinoha-zushi (a local favourite) contains fish.

cities.name: Koyasan
cities.season: Cool in summer, snowy in winter; temple stays all year.
cities.culture: A mountain-top monastery town where you can sleep in a temple and join morning prayers.
cities.veg: Temple lodgings serve shojin ryori, traditionally free of meat, fish, onion and garlic. Tell them early if you are Jain.

cities.name: Osaka
cities.season: Lively all year; neon Dotonbori is best at night.
cities.culture: Japan's kitchen: street food, comedy and a friendly, loud crowd.
cities.veg: Indian restaurants are easy to find, but classic street food uses octopus, pork or dashi (takoyaki, okonomiyaki).

cities.name: Hiroshima
cities.season: Pleasant spring and autumn; pairs with Miyajima.
cities.culture: The Peace Memorial Park and a city rebuilt around a message of peace.
cities.veg: Hiroshima okonomiyaki usually has pork and dashi; some places make a vegetarian version on request.

cities.name: Miyajima
cities.fromTokyo: About 4.5 h via Hiroshima and ferry
cities.season: See the floating torii at high tide; check tide tables.
cities.culture: The island of Itsukushima Shrine and its great torii standing in the sea.
cities.veg: Momiji manju (maple-leaf cakes) are vegetarian; the oysters and eel the island is known for are not.

cities.name: Fukuoka
cities.fromTokyo: About 5 h by Shinkansen or 2 h by air
cities.season: Mild winters; open-air yatai stalls every evening.
cities.culture: A relaxed coastal city, gateway to Kyushu's hot springs and volcanoes.
cities.veg: The capital of tonkotsu (pork-bone) ramen, so be careful; look for vegan ramen and Indian restaurants instead.

cities.name: Sapporo
cities.season: Snow Festival in February; flower fields in July.
cities.culture: Wide streets, snow sculptures and Hokkaido's countryside on the doorstep.
cities.veg: Soup curry can be made vegetarian at some shops; ramen broths are usually pork or seafood.

cities.name: Okinawa (Naha)
cities.season: Beach season April to October; typhoons possible late summer.
cities.culture: Subtropical islands with their own Ryukyu culture, music and crafts.
cities.veg: Champuru stir-fries usually include pork or egg; tofu, sweet potato and sea grapes are good options to ask about.
